summary: Federal Communications Commission proposes rulemaking to modify E-Rate program, which school districts rely on for broadband connectivity. School districts urge preservation of E-Rate program to maintain essential connectivity infrastructure and avoid increased operational costs. FCC proposal to sunset or reduce E-Rate support is opposed by school districts as it would impose additional financial burdens on local budgets and compromise cybersecurity measures. The school district argues against sunsetting or eliminating the E-Rate program, emphasizing its importance for maintaining reliable broadband infrastructure in schools and libraries. They urge the Commission to preserve E-Rate support and reject proposals that would narrow eligibility or restrict support based on geography.

claims.argument: Reducing E-Rate would shift connectivity costs to local taxpayers, increasing operational burdens on school budgets
claims.evidence_quote: With cyberattacks and data breaches posing a constant threat to schools, reducing this support would make it more difficult and more expensive for districts to protect student information and maintain safe, reliable systems

claims.requested_action: Reject proposals to sunset or eliminate the E-Rate program
claims.argument: Reducing E-Rate support based on location would widen existing learning gaps
claims.evidence_quote: I therefore respectfully urge the Commission to: Reject any proposal to sunset or eliminate the E-Rate program; Reject proposals that would unnecessarily narrow E-Rate eligibility or restrict support based solely on geography or other criteria that would leave students without adequate support
